body:
Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement with Statistical Guarantees

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.10787

Recursive self-improvement offers a promising path toward AI agents that improve through experience by refining their own harnesses without retraining their underlying large language models (LLMs). Making this self-improvement process reliable, however, requires more than generating new updates: agents must decide which changes are worth keeping. A greedy gate that accepts updates based solely on higher validation scores can mistake an observed gain for genuine progress and lead to performance degeneration, whereas overly conservative statistical gates may reject beneficial updates and hinder performance improvement. We introduce Trustworthy Recursive Updates with Statistical Testing (TRUST), a framework that adapts an online multiple hypothesis testing procedure to control the rate of false evolution across rounds, with an LLM analyzing historical context to help determine how much evidence is required to update the incumbent. Under interpretable assumptions, we prove that TRUST limits the proportion of accepted updates that result in unacceptable performance loss. We further derive a lower bound on the final performance gain. Across the benchmarks HotpotQA, DROP, and APPS with the models DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Qwen-3.8-Flash, TRUST reduces the average ratio of accepted inferior updates from the greedy gate's 45.59% to 2.78%, while achieving higher final scores than the state-of-the-art statistical gate baselines for recursive self-improvement. These findings demonstrate that TRUST strikes a balance between statistical reliability and performance gain in recursive self-improvement.
title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement with Statistical Guarantees

body:
Task-adaptive anonymisation enables privacy-preserving sharing of clinical speech data

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11273

Clinical speech is increasingly used for disease screening and clinical assessment, but directly distributing speech recordings poses privacy risks because they contain both speaker-identifying voiceprints and sensitive spoken content. Existing speech anonymisation approaches are primarily developed for general speech applications or task-specific clinical speech and overlook that different clinical tasks rely on distinct speech characteristics, necessitating task-adaptive anonymisation strategies to protect patient privacy while preserving clinical utility. Here we introduce CASA, a clinically adaptive speech anonymisation agent that transforms anonymisation from a fixed processing procedure into a task-guided optimisation process, dynamically tailoring voiceprint and content anonymisation to task-specific privacy and clinical utility requirements. Through recursive self-improvement (RSI), CASA iteratively evaluates and refines anonymisation strategies against task-specific privacy and clinical utility requirements, while learning from these outcomes to guide more efficient planning in subsequent clinical tasks. CASA is validated across 14 clinical tasks encompassing five languages, diverse elicitation paradigms, and mental health, cognitive and voice disorders. CASA preserved disease-related classification performance while meeting speaker-anonymisation requirements across all clinical tasks, versus only 8/14 for the strongest fixed method. Assessments of resistance to speaker re-identification by external attackers and identification and redaction of sensitive personal information in clinical speech further demonstrated CASA's dual protection of speaker identity and sensitive spoken content. Clinical expert assessments further supported the preservation of clinically relevant information and the acceptability of anonymised speech for controlled research sharing.
title: Task-adaptive anonymisation enables privacy-preserving sharing of clinical speech data

body:
JoMoHa: Joint Model--Harness Optimization with Reinforcement Learning

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11499

The performance of language agents depends jointly on model weights and the harness. Optimizing either alone can be constrained by the other component, limiting overall performance gains. Our analysis of naive alternating training reveals progressive incompatibility between the model and harness, which increasingly interferes with task execution and may also undermine model training, leading to performance degradation. To coordinate the evolution of models and harnesses, we introduce JoMoHa, to our knowledge the first framework to jointly train an executable harness generation policy and a task execution policy through reinforcement learning. JoMoHa outperforms the evaluated weight-only and harness-only baselines and achieves the highest success rates among the evaluated methods on ALFWorld, WebShop, and DBBench, averaging 70.3% and reaching 97.0% on ALFWorld. By learning both task execution and runtime improvement from its own generated trajectories, JoMoHa performs recursive self-improvement (RSI).
title: JoMoHa: Joint Model--Harness Optimization with Reinforcement Learning

body:
Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11509

Recent studies of embodied agents based on frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) develop harness engineering around the MLLM, such as harnesses with post-trained policies and recursive self-improvement loops. Yet whether these additions exceed the native capability of the MLLM remains unexplored. We introduce SimplEvo to explore how far an MLLM can improve under direct control when it retains its execution experience in self-written text memories. It requires no weight updates, post-trained policies, or privileged information. The MLLM writes a coordinate-free task memory once from a single demonstration. Under a strict train-test protocol, it then creates a bounded working memory on training episodes only and refines it after each episode with lessons on procedure, completion, and recovery. Both memories stay fixed at test time. On EBench, SimplEvo lifts the success rate (SR) of GPT-6-Astra under direct control from 46.7% to 81.7%, and tops the RoboDojo leaderboard with 69.63% SR and a score of 75.32. Compared with memories that also store past visual frames, SimplEvo reaches a similar SR with text memory alone while using fewer tokens. With its memories fixed, SimplEvo also generalizes to unseen layouts and randomized scene configurations. Moreover, the working memory transfers across models: written by GPT-6-Astra, it can be reused as is by weaker MLLMs and improve their performance without any adaptation of their own.
title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents

body:
InfraRSI: Harnessing Recursive Self-Improvement for Training Infrastructure

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11558

While Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) accelerates isolated algorithm and kernel synthesis, distributed LLM training depends on tightly coupled launch settings, operator kernels, and communication schedules, where single edits often hit out-of-memory (OOM) boundaries, compiler conflicts, measurement jitter, or silent numerical drift. We present InfraRSI, the agentic harness that turns open-ended human commands into verified training optimizations via a five-stage workflow: init locks editable scope and a fixed task contract over workload, loss, and timing invariants to prevent reward hacking, doctor profiles baseline phases and calibrates cluster noise, run co-optimizes launch knobs and code patches before re-verifying top candidates against the baseline and logging findings to a cross-hardware experience bank, and report and apply audit source paths, track failed-trial costs, and commit promoted changes. Rather than stepping greedily from a single incumbent, InfraRSI initializes from diverse experience-seeded configurations and fits global execution-time and censored peak-memory models across all trials, including OOMs. Using these models, it prices per-setting memory costs, revises miscalibrated LLM priors from live runs, and pairs memory-hungry optimizations with memory savers and verified code patches. Across four single- and multi-node dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLM workloads, InfraRSI achieves a speedup of up to $2.75\times$ and lifts mean Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU) from $17.4\%$ to $30.0\%$, outperforming existing tuners and coding agents while transferring experience across GPUs. As it improves training infrastructure efficiency, InfraRSI forms a two-level Recursive Self-Improvement loop---revising priors online within runs and distilling experience across clusters---to push foundation model scaling.
title: InfraRSI: Harnessing Recursive Self-Improvement for Training Infrastructure

body:
ForgeSystem: An Architecture for Demand-Specific Artefact Production with AI Agents

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12288

General-purpose software serves many different demands, but this flexibility costs performance and efficiency on any specific demand. Software tailored to a specific demand avoids these losses, yet developing it requires substantial time and effort from human experts. AI agents offer an alternative: they can design, implement and test artefacts tailored to individual demands. We call this production paradigm Forge. Forging for a demand is economically justified when the cumulative benefit of specialisation exceeds the total cost of construction, verification and maintenance. To make Forge a repeatable production process, we propose ForgeSystem, which consists of a control layer, a forge loop and a recursive self-improvement (RSI) loop. The control layer selects which artefact serves each demand and decides which demands to forge, when to forge them and from which starting point; the forge loop iterates between production and verification until a candidate artefact passes verification; and the RSI loop draws on accumulated production records to supply starting points, refine the harness and train models. We implement ForgeSystem for training frameworks, decoding megakernels and individual computational kernels. Forged training engines reach 1.047-1.332x the model-FLOPs utilisation of their reference frameworks, forged megakernels achieve a geometric-mean decoding speedup of 1.21x over SGLang across thirteen configurations, and forged kernels match or exceed expert libraries in eighteen of twenty-two configurations, while satisfying task-specific quality requirements. Controlled comparisons show that explicit quality requirements steer agents towards optimisations that preserve training quality. We also discuss a gradual transition to Forge through service routing, and how demand-specific production may shift value accumulation and trust towards production systems.
title: ForgeSystem: An Architecture for Demand-Specific Artefact Production with AI Agents

body:
SciMARS: Multi-Agent Recursive Self-Improvement for Closed-Loop Scientific Discovery

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12552

We propose SciMARS, a framework for recursive task-local adaptation of multi-agent harnesses in closed-loop scientific discovery. Multi-agent systems coordinate analysis, experimental design, and verification as scientific evidence evolves. However, two problems limit their effectiveness: (i) without shared memory, agents lose observations and repeat work; (ii) fixed role procedures, handoffs, and memory policies perpetuate mistakes despite retained evidence. We address these problems with a shared evidence graph and separate component editors. SciMARS adapts roles and coordination; SciMARS + Memory adds a third editor for how agents record, retrieve, and receive evidence. Candidate probes guide composition and selection of the next harness. We evaluate scientific discovery through experimental-data replay and a digital twin. SciMARS + Memory resolves 12/18 GPT-6-Astra and 2/18 GLM-5.3 attempts on Autonomous Science Bench, compared with 8/18 and 1/18 for the base multi-agent team. On ScienceAgentBench and AppWorld, it solves 14/38 and 11/20 tasks, compared with 11/38 and 5/20 for the base team. These results support combining shared memory with harness adaptation across scientific and interactive tasks.
title: SciMARS: Multi-Agent Recursive Self-Improvement for Closed-Loop Scientific Discovery

body:
The RSI Tax: When Recursive Self-Improvement Is Not Worth the Cost

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13524

Recursive self-improvement (RSI) seeks to improve an agent using its own task experience. Its practical value depends on whether performance gains justify the full cost of self-improvement and task execution. We evaluate this trade-off on continual task streams, scoring each task before its feedback is used for subsequent updates. We define the \emph{RSI Tax} as the token cost of the self-improvement process and include it alongside task-execution costs in end-to-end evaluation. Across six methods and two language models, a bounded-note baseline matches or exceeds the observed accuracy of Meta-Harness, EvoSkill, and RRSI, with mean total-token savings of 65.6-71.0\%. We decompose the RSI Tax into verification, exploration, and writing costs, and track subsequent use of the associated state or artifact. For these three RSI methods, verification accounts for 74.8--93.6% of the aggregate RSI Tax. A substantial share of the RSI Tax is also associated with states or artifacts that are not used later in the evaluated streams. These results expose a practical limitation of costly RSI procedures: improvements in the deployed agent need not justify the expense of the improvement process. They motivate RSI objectives that jointly optimize the RSI Tax and expected task-execution cost while ensuring continued growth in agent capabilities across the task stream.
title: The RSI Tax: When Recursive Self-Improvement Is Not Worth the Cost

body:
WAM is capable in BEHAVIOR-1K: the 2nd-place solution to the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13818

This work presents the 2nd-place solution (Team IF1001) to the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge, which evaluates mobile manipulation across 100 household tasks. Our method is built on a powerful world action model (WAM), Cosmos 3. We improve Cosmos 3 by using richer visual history, task-progress conditioning, and task-group and skill-specific LoRA adapters. During inference, we apply a separate progress estimator to supply task-progress context, and use task- and progress-conditioned routing to select a task-group or skill-specific policy, complemented by action-candidate aggregation, rolling inpainting, and task-specific temporal and gripper control. To meet the minimum inference requirement of 1 FPS, we use neither recursive self-improvement (RSI) nor agentic harness methods and rely on no closed-source models; during official private-test evaluation, our system handled concurrent requests across 100 evaluation ports with limited hardware resources, sustaining an average end-to-end inference rate above 2 FPS per port. Our method achieves a mean Q-score of 0.613 and a full-task success rate of 40.9%, averaged over 3 self-evaluation rounds across all 100 tasks. On the official private test set, with 20 instances per task, our system achieves a mean Q-score of 0.615 and a full-task success rate of 41.2%.
title: WAM is capable in BEHAVIOR-1K: the 2nd-place solution to the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge

body:
RSI-PDEbench: A Benchmark for Self-Improving Agents in PDE Solving

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14949

Identifying and solving partial differential equations (PDEs) from sampled solution data often requires substantial expert effort in equation discovery, coefficient estimation, and numerical solver configuration, especially under noise and distribution shifts. Can large language model (LLM) agents automate this workflow accurately and efficiently? To investigate this question, we introduce \bench{}, a benchmark of 1,001 cases spanning 42 equation templates, including both classical and fractional PDEs. It provides three evaluation settings: Full evaluates performance on noise-free solution data; Noisy tests robustness to Gaussian noise with an RMS equal to 50\% of the clean-signal RMS; and Hard-OOD tests challenging out-of-distribution generalization to unseen equation templates and shifted coefficient ranges. We further introduce RSI-PDE, a recursively self-improving agent harness that shortlists candidate equations by residual loss, uses relative $L^2$ feedback to refine coefficients and numerical solvers, and applies a validation gate to policy and memory updates. We compare RSI-PDE with single-run baselines and native agent harnesses (Claude Code or Codex) across four frontier models. Across the three settings, RSI-PDE improves the pass rate averaged across the four models by 106.5--181.9\% relative to single-run baselines and by 3.0--19.6\% relative to native harnesses, while reducing total recorded model calls by 46.9\% across the 12 model--setting pairs. These results highlight the potential of validated recursive self-improvement in LLM agents to advance scientific computing.
title: RSI-PDEbench: A Benchmark for Self-Improving Agents in PDE Solving

body:
MULTILOOP: Evolving Multi-Agent Harnesses for Complex Information-Seeking Tasks

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15754

The performance of LLM-based agents depends not only on the underlying model but also on the harness: the prompts, tools, and orchestration logic around it. Recent works automate harness optimization with coding agents that analyze execution traces, diagnose failures, and edit the harness code; however, those focused on single-agent systems. Multi-agent harnesses are harder to optimize as fixing them requires changing how agents interact in addition to how each behaves. We study whether automated harness optimization can diagnose and repair failures in multi-agent systems through a case study on complex information-seeking tasks from DeepSearchQA [Gupta et al., 2026]. We apply MULTILOOP, a simple optimization loop in which a coding agent iteratively analyzes, evaluates and edits the harness. With only 10 training samples, the evolved harness improves accuracy by 4.6% over the base harness and by 3.2% over the best single-agent system. However, a taxonomy of failure modes before and after optimization shows that the orchestration failures that characterize multi-agent systems largely persist. Our findings motivate harness optimization methods that encourage structural changes to how agents delegate tasks and share information.
title: MULTILOOP: Evolving Multi-Agent Harnesses for Complex Information-Seeking Tasks

body:
Experience-Handoff Reinforcement Learning for Recursive Self-Improvement

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16409

It is common to train Large Language Models (LLMs) for agentic tasks with Reinforcement Learning (RL) from scalar rewards. However, this throws away the fine-grained information about the environment that the agent experienced during the trial (e.g., error logs). To utilize this rich information, recent works wrap the agent in a harness that refines its own inputs through reflection or compaction and hands past experience to future rollouts, but the construction of the handed-off artifacts (e.g., a playbook) is itself not learned. We want the best of both worlds: gradient updates from a scalar reward, while also utilizing environment information to hand off experience. As a concrete testbed, we fix the Agentic Context Engineering (\ace{}) harness and train one model to act, reflect, and curate task-local playbooks. Our method, \acerl{}, evaluates candidate experience-handoff artifacts by their downstream effect on future actor rollouts, and co-optimizes the role-specific behaviors (action generator, insight reflector, and playbook curator) under a fixed scaffold. Across agentic benchmarks, \acerl{} achieves higher held-out performance than baseline methods. The results suggest that agent training should optimize not only the actions in the current rollout, but also the model-written experience that future rollouts inherit.
title: Experience-Handoff Reinforcement Learning for Recursive Self-Improvement

body:
AutoRL: A Multi-Agent System towards Autonomous Reinforcement Learning

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17790

Recursive self-improvement (RSI) is one of the most promising paths toward an AI singularity for superintelligence. Achieving this vision requires AI systems to undertake the full training pipeline for iterative improvement. Reinforcement learning (RL) plays an essential role in this cycle to improve model capabilities and generalization, yet automating RL remains difficult due to unstable training dynamics and the need for sustained supervision. We introduce AutoRL, a multi-agent system for automating RL training, as a cornerstone for future RSI. Different from conducting research by end-to-end complete experiments, AutoRL monitors the evolving training state and integrates process-level supervision and research into an ongoing RL training, following the practical workflow of an RL researcher. Specifically, AutoRL consists of three RL-specific agentic roles. Perceptors track training dynamics, rollouts, evaluation, and efficiency, triggering deliberation when they detect anomalies, degradation, or stagnation. Three complementary Proposers diagnose problems and refine candidate interventions through shared evidence and checks. The Orchestrator reviews their recommendation and applies approved changes through online hot updates or checkpoint-based resumption. Experiments on Qwen3 and LongCat-Flash-Lite demonstrate the superiority of AutoRL over static RL recipes and a general agent. The research records show that existing agents can handle unattended RL supervision and dynamic adjustment. The difficulty for future RSI lies in developing fundamental methods that are valuable for resource-consuming validation.
title: AutoRL: A Multi-Agent System towards Autonomous Reinforcement Learning

body:
G-CAST: Governed Continual Self-Training for E-Commerce Agents under Evolving Demands

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17814

With the rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs), an increasing number of users are turning to LLM-powered agents for conversational shopping in e-commerce. However, the user needs continue to change as new product categories, procurement scenarios, and feature requests emerge. At the same time, the product's execution harness-including its tools, skills, and operating procedures-continues to evolve to support increasingly sophisticated interactions. These changes create two practical challenges: 1) Demand drift alters the distribution, intent, and complexity of user requests, causing a model trained once to fall behind; 2) Harness evolution requires the model to use newly introduced capabilities correctly without losing behavior that users already rely on. Periodic manual retraining is too delayed and labor-intensive for this setting. To address these challenges, we present G-CAST, a governed continual self-training system that converts daily production evidence under evolving demand and capability contracts into reward-routed, entropy-prioritized training data and governed reward evolution. Governed checkpoint transition under cumulative evaluation controls each model update, enabling the agent to learn newly introduced behaviors without sacrificing previously accepted capabilities. Experiments on a real production e-commerce agent show that G-CAST achieves stronger adaptation to newly introduced demand while better preserving previously accepted behavior compared with a strong autonomous post-training baseline. Ablations further show that both reward-routed, entropy-prioritized data orchestration and governed reward evolution are important to these gains. G-CAST is now deployed in Yuancai(http://cai.1688.com/), a B2B procurement agent on Alibaba's 1688 platform.
title: G-CAST: Governed Continual Self-Training for E-Commerce Agents under Evolving Demands

body:
RecurIR: Learning When and How to Revise Restoration Policies via Recursive Self-Improvement

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18006

Agent-based image restoration has achieved promising performance by coordinating restoration tools to handle heterogeneous and coupled degradations. However, existing agents often improve their decisions through accumulated successful and failed executions, without explicitly identifying the conditions under which learned restoration strategies remain effective. Consequently, changes in degradation severity, spatial coverage, or interactions may invalidate previous decisions, while providing limited guidance on how these decisions should be revised. In this paper, we propose \textbf{RecurIR}, a recursive self-improvement framework that enables restoration agents to learn when and how to revise their decision rules. Specifically, we introduce a policy-hypothesis discovery mechanism to identify testable, condition-dependent rules through matched tool executions. We then design a rule-falsification-driven task evolution mechanism to generate targeted degradation variations, examine the validity of learned rules, and identify their applicability boundaries. Based on the resulting evidence, we develop a change-conditioned policy revision mechanism that learns how variations in degradation conditions should modify tool selection, execution order, operation strength, and processing regions. We further incorporate independent verification to retain effective revisions and use the resulting feedback to guide subsequent hypothesis discovery and task evolution. Through this recursive process, RecurIR progressively refines its restoration policies as degradation conditions change. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
title: RecurIR: Learning When and How to Revise Restoration Policies via Recursive Self-Improvement

- [ ] **Reflective Compositional Grounding for Natural-Language-to-SPARQL** `arxiv:2610.21796`：需核实：(1) 是否存在跨问题/跨会话保存并复用被接受要求集或映射库（M_t/H_t）的实际实现与实验；(2) 提示重写是否保留显式、累积的规格而非一次性文本重写；(3) 后续版本或附录是否新增跨查询保留评估。若仅有任务内提示重写，则应归为 other_direction 并排除。
- [ ] **BetaMem: Learning to Remember a Changing World for Embodied Agents** `arxiv:2610.26554`：核对附录或实验是否实际运行 Algorithm 1，是否报告 held-out replay、接受/拒绝的修复、rollback 与后续 episode 复用；确认 RSI 对 benchmark 的独立贡献，并确认权重在该子机制中固定且非主要干预。
- [ ] **Automated Multi-Agent Organization Design: From Architecture Search to Organizational Learning** `arxiv:2610.27531`：检查是否存在附录/实验章节或后续版本给出实际运行结果（跨仓库 CooperBench、MultiAgentBench、ChinaTravel 上的成功率、修订次数、成本）；确认是否有任何已验证职责经组织记忆在后续任务中被检索、重验证并复用（即真正的跨任务持久化证据）；确认设计者 π_θ 的参数来源——若设计者本身通过 SFT/RL 训练且为主要干预，则需重新评估是否滑向权重优化而非 Harness。
- [ ] **Cache Engineering for Agents** `arxiv:2610.28577`：需核对图 4 及附录：(a) RSI 中被修改的策略以何种可落盘、可复用的形式存在（系统提示 / 配置文件 / 代码），是否成为后续任务默认使用的工件；(b) 评估反馈（成本、准确率、失败轨迹）如何具体转化为策略修改，候选由谁生成、如何筛选与保留；(c) 改进后的策略是否在后续会话/优化轮次中继承并复用于非 BCP 任务；(d) 明确区分“AKV 服务引擎优化”与“agent 自身缓存管理策略演化”哪一个是论文的主要干预对象。
- [ ] **SpatialBrain: Spatial Intelligence Growing from Experience** `arxiv:2610.29317`：查实际被新编译并接受、后续使用的 procedure diff/run trace，避免把支持统计更新当作程序演化。
- [ ] **Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting** `arxiv:2610.29784`：需要 skill 文件或实际可复用策略工件的创建/修订/保留证据，不能以 paper 中 skill 一词自动通过，也不能仅因 GRPO 自动排除。
- [ ] **CANNBot-CAKE: Collaborative Agentic Kernel Evolution for Ascend NPU** `arxiv:2610.31034`：需要核实：(a) 仓库/附录中是否存在具体的已合并 PR 或 skill-editor 产出，能追踪到一次由评测反馈触发的 skill/prompt/repair-template/router 改动及其对后续算子成功率的对照影响；(b) PMR 产出的策略规则是否实际被加入策略库并用于其他算子，是否有前后对比；(c) CAKE Book 条目经"promotion"进入静态参考后是否观测到行为改变；(d) router 的跨算子路由变化是否可作为对外部可复用策略工件的持续更新证据（而非仅对历史得分排序）。
- [ ] **ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation** `arxiv:2610.32120`：需要区分经验内容与可复用程序变异，并隔离 judge 权重训练相对外部程序改写的主次；保留 defer。
- [ ] **Build, Don't Play: Self-Improving LLM Research Agents Develop a Hearthstone Battlegrounds AI That Rivals Top Players** `arxiv:2610.33845`：需核查：新增验证门与常设规则是否以机器可读/可执行的工作流或配置文件形式持久化并自动对后续 session 生效，而非仅作为记忆条目被读取；是否存在任何量化证据把“研究过程自改进”与模拟器保真度、对手校准、PPO 权重的贡献分离；以及该机制是否超出边界 (b)（仅记忆条目的存取/加载）。
- [ ] **Infinity Machine: a self-improving AI agent for research** `arxiv:2610.35579`：核查省略正文或附录中是否存在通过 gate 并持久化的工具、技能、playbook 或 meta-agent 代际，以及这些改动是否在后续任务/会话中被复用；若无，则应排除。
- [ ] **Instant Software Factories** `arxiv:2610.36254`：核查后续版本是否报告 bootstrap 在多个仓库上的执行评估、反馈驱动的 prompt/例程修改，以及修改后工件在后续任务或会话中的持久复用与改进；若仍只是人工蒸馏或未来计划，则不应计入。
- [ ] **Evolving Agent Teams** `arxiv:2610.36848`：需核查：(a) 进化出的团队配置、supervisor prompt、LEARNINGS.md/SYNTHESIS.md 是否以可复用文件形式保存，并在新任务或新会话中被加载复用（而非每次 from scratch 重建）；(b) 是否存在跨任务的迁移实验，显示同一进化后的编排/知识管理策略在后续任务上被直接使用并改进；(c) 正文 Section 3 与 Appendix 中 K 的生命周期定义（每任务独立还是全局）；(d) 若仅为任务内多轮团队重构，则应归为 other_direction（任务输出驱动的搜索过程适配）。
- [ ] **AgentDiscover: Autonomous Discovery with Minimal Search Scaffolding** `arxiv:2610.05334`：跨独立发现问题的 Harness 保留或明确说明该问题内会话满足收录边界
- [ ] **MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents** `arxiv:2610.13829`：一般程序性经验规则与 Harness 专项评测的编辑范围判定
- [ ] **What May an Agent Change About Itself? A Containment Floor for Self-Configuring Agent Runtimes** `arxiv:2610.06274`：Containment Floor 检查 Agent 通过自身配置工具写持久 manifest 扩权的安全边界；配置下次启动生效，是真外部控制工件，但实验由普通配置请求触发，固定六规则无性能反馈演化，meta-agent 部分明确仅设计论证。可相关安全阅读，暂不称完整 Harness RSI 专项实验。
- [ ] **MemCo: Memory-Centric Collaboration for Generalizing LLM Agents to Unseen Environments** `arxiv:2610.07376`：MemCo 的 typed global memory 含行为顺序、前置条件和修复规则，按各 episode 执行证据晋级/删除并跨任务复用，再渲染为当前动作指导，不能当纯事实记忆。但存取/门槛/渲染机制固定，变的是结构化记忆内容而非独立版本控制程序；暂保程序性记忆与 Harness 技能边界，交 root 按当前专题口径裁定。
- [ ] **Agent Sociodrama: Social-Dynamics-Guided Persona Recasting for LLM Agent Teams** `arxiv:2610.15788`：TPR 的角色重分配是根据多轮真实交互反馈调整的持久 casting，不能说只有情绪状态变化；但正文仍固定同一任务情景/私有知识，反复测同一情景，未见跨独立任务保留或迁移。维持待补，不将循环存在直接当成 Harness 核心证据。
- [ ] **JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs** `arxiv:2610.21412`：JevAgentHarness 从真实 shadow-mode 任务轨迹拟合持久路由阈值、固定脚本选组合后新任务测试，不能说纯权重工作；但外部机制是预设统计校准，未见反复修改规则/提示/程序的闭环。暂待 core 口径裁定，SFT/GRPO 分列。
- [ ] **A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft** `arxiv:2610.22319`：独立任务／新 run 可复用技能及其保留接口。
- [ ] **D-Skill: Distilling Teacher Knowledge through Agent Skills** `arxiv:2610.28914`：主审核需决定是否仅以SkillOpt-backed子实验作为Harness组件收录依据；未决定前formal defer。

- [ ] **Evolver: Turning Agent Exploration into Evolving Capabilities** `arxiv:2611.07595`：Original full-text methods and experiment scope required before acceptance.
- [ ] **Avatar Intelligence: Amplifying Human Agency Through Persistent Personal Agents** `arxiv:2611.03092`：第4.2节明确提出跨episode的用户情境Rehearsal Engineering，更新记忆、技能选择和决策策略，不能说它没有反馈演化；全文主题仍是个人Agent个性化、授权与监督的一般议程，不是Harness演化专项。建议留为通用RSI相关理论。

body:
OmniBrain-0: A Unified Agentic Model for Embodied Intelligence

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36013

General-purpose embodied intelligence requires robots to coordinate diverse skills over long horizons, track task progress, and recover from failures. Specialist policies alone do not ensure task-level reliability, while powerful multimodal agents rely on costly reasoning and external experience that compact models struggle to reproduce. We introduce OmniBrain-0, a lightweight unified embodied agent that coordinates manipulation and navigation through a shared high-level decision model, integrating task understanding, planning, progress tracking, and feedback-driven recovery. Our progressive training framework combines embodied pretraining, domain-specialized agent distillation, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). It distills powerful teachers' interaction experience into manipulation and navigation experts, then consolidates their decision capabilities into OmniBrain-0. Unification therefore occurs within the learned decision model rather than only at the tool interface. We further introduce Rubric-Guided Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI), a data flywheel in which a Meta-Agent turns execution evidence into refined rubrics, step-level reminders, and verified trajectories for domain-expert updates before their reconsolidation into OmniBrain-0 through MOPD. We evaluate OmniBrain-0 on LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-Plus, RoboCasa365, RoboTwin 2.0, and R2R-CE Val-Unseen, as well as multiple real-world manipulation tasks. OmniBrain-0 combines strong cross-domain task performance with substantially lower inference and execution overhead than its closed-source teacher, demonstrating efficient transfer and consolidation of embodied capabilities into a compact unified agent.
title: OmniBrain-0: A Unified Agentic Model for Embodied Intelligence

body:
VEvo-Harness: Causally-Guarded Self-Evolving Harness for Agentic Image Generation

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39158

The central bottleneck in visual generation and editing has migrated from achieving pixel-level fidelity to satisfying densely constrained user specifications through increasingly agentic workflows. Prevailing agentic generation pipelines remain shallow generate-verify-rewrite loops treating VLM judgments as coarse visual feedback, either discarding repair experience or admitting ungated updates that poison skill library. With memorize and govern periods left open, they degrade into ungoverned iterators of repeated trial-and-error rather than continual self-evolving harness. Towards this issue, we present \textbf{VEvo-Harness}, the first causally-guarded continual self-evolving harness system for agentic visual generation. VEvo-Harness introduces four coupled innovations: (1) \textit{a visual traceback} that densifies sparse judgments into root-cause attributions with a hierarchical verification tree; (2) \textit{a visual continual governance} that admits only causally valid skill patches through counterfactual dual-arm image generation replay; (3) \textit{a lifecycle-managed harness state} that hierarchically distills root-cause-anchored episodes across working, experience, and pattern tiers into a persistent skill library of routable and causally verified capabilities; (4) \textit{a heterogeneous sandbox policy} that orchestrates a diverse action space of repair primitives, dynamically routing cost-aware interventions based on root causes to select the most effective strategy. VEvo-Harness surpasses state-of-the-art agentic methods and rivals proprietary generators (\textit{e.g.}, GPT-Image, Nano-Pro) while maintaining the continual harness evolution and generalization.
title: VEvo-Harness: Causally-Guarded Self-Evolving Harness for Agentic Image Generation

body:
MoLRSI: A Recursive Self-Improving AI agent for Molecular Discovery

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39714

Molecular discovery requires navigating vast combinatorial search spaces while balancing competing biological objectives. AI agents can automate expert-defined molecular design protocols, but automation alone does not address how to optimize workflows for new tasks or improve their development through experience. Here we introduce MoLRSI, an AI agent that combines systematic optimization of workflows and model architectures with persistent cross-task memory to recursively improve its search policy for molecular discovery. Workflow performance, refinement outcomes, and execution feedback guide subsequent searches, allowing the agent to improve both its workflows and its strategy for developing them. We evaluate MoLRSI in two challenging molecular discovery settings that require balancing competing properties. In antibiotic discovery, MoLRSI developed a screening workflow balancing antibacterial activity, cytotoxicity and structural novelty, achieving an experimental hit rate of 15.9%, compared with 8.7% for a previous expert-led workflow using the same training data and screening library. In de novo peptide-MHC binder design, MoLRSI developed workflows that jointly consider target binding and specificity, producing eight experimentally validated hits against MART-1 and SARS-CoV-1 pMHCs with preferential binding over tested off-targets while Claude Science completely failed. These findings demonstrate how experience-guided workflow optimization can address competing discovery objectives while improving the search strategies used in subsequent campaigns.
title: MoLRSI: A Recursive Self-Improving AI agent for Molecular Discovery

body:
KARMA: Training-Free Knowledge-Atomic Harness Evolution for Industrial Advertising Agents

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39884

Industrial advertising agents must continually adapt their decision knowledge to changing product offerings, traffic patterns, and operating policies. We present KARMA (Knowledge-Atomic, Regression-Gated Modular Adaptation), a training-free framework that evolves six typed knowledge modules while keeping model weights and executable harness code frozen. During our evolution, a deterministic Trace Verifier maps observed errors to candidate modules, and a Critic compares successful and failed trajectories to guide a tool-constrained Evolver. The Evolver applies atomic knowledge edits, which a fixed validation gate retains only when their measured gain reaches a threshold; otherwise, the previous knowledge state is restored. We evaluate KARMA with three LLM families on cases sampled from a corpus of approximately half a million real-world operation logs across six e-commerce domains. Across 18 domain--model settings, KARMA raises the average hold-out score from 30.19 to 39.15 (+8.96 points, +29.7%). Ablations show that removing either successful or failed trajectories more than halves the average hold-out gain. Evolved knowledge also transfers across domains without further adaptation, yielding an average hold-out gain of 8.54 points across all source--target pairs. By linking retained patches to their diagnostic evidence and validation outcomes, KARMA supports inspectable, reversible knowledge adaptation for agents in Web marketplaces.
title: KARMA: Training-Free Knowledge-Atomic Harness Evolution for Industrial Advertising Agents
